newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania Senate gives foreigners right to own land.
newsitem.headline: Romania Senate gives foreigners right to own land.

text.p: Romania's Senate has passed after hot debates a bill granting foreigners the right to own land in Romania, likely to boost foreign investments in the Balkan country, an official said on Tuesday.

Under the bill, foreign-owned local companies or firms with partly foreign capital are given "the right of property and any other real rights over the land they need to carry out their activity during their existence here."
The Senate, parliament's upper house, passed the bill with 80 votes for and 50 against amid "very animated and vehement" debates, a Senate official said.
"Many of those who opposed the bill actually reiterated the old slogan 'We don't sell out our country'. But times are changing," the official, who asked not to be named, said.
To become effective the bill also needs approval from parliament's lower Chamber of Deputies.
"The new bill is clearly an incentive for foreign investors," the official said.

Under a 1991 foreign investment law, foreigners may own land through local companies having at least one Romanian shareholder. This was perceived as one of the major hindrances to foreign investments in Romania.

The bill passed by the Senate on Tuesday is part of moves by the new centrist government headed by Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea, which ousted the former leftist cabinet in elections last November, to smash barriers to foreign investment.
"I am confident the bill will clear the other house in its present form," the official said in reference to the vote of the centrist-dominated Chamber of Deputies.
Romania hopes foreign investment will pick up this year as the new government pledged to support foreign investors by boosting facilities, granting tax cuts and fighting red tape.
Total direct foreign investment since the 19989 overthrow of communist rule amounts to a little over $2.0 billion.

Last month, the state-run news agency Rompres said a study on Romania's economy by the Integral Consultancy Service (IBD) of Germany ran on 1,800 German existing and potential investors in Romania had cited "the unclear situation of the right to purchase land" among the obstacles preventing foreign investors from coming to this country.
